_comment: The family's own words about the people who cooked. Printed on each cook's page exactly as written. (All fictional.)

Demo-Daly-9.story: Hannah raised six children on a farm outside Skibbereen and, family tradition says, never wasted a crust. When the two youngest left for Boston she is said to have baked bread for a week to give them something to carry.

Demo-Murphy-4.story: Patrick sailed from Cork at sixteen with an address on a scrap of paper. He worked the Boston docks for forty years and never once, his daughter Mary said, came home without something for the table.

Demo-Walsh-5.story: Nora crossed the Atlantic in 1919 to marry a man she had met twice. She kept a recipe box she never let anyone else touch, and half of what is in it is in her own hand.

Demo-Brandt-7.story: Greta grew up in Hartford, the daughter of German bakers, and brought the Christmas baking to Worcester when she married.
